subject.title: fix(agents): keep multimodal models when generated catalogs include audio/video inputs

question: Should OpenClaw accept audio/video as additive runtime model input metadata for generated provider catalogs, and should this PR become the canonical landing path after the Codex preservation gap is fixed?
rationale: The code repair is mechanical, but choosing a widened provider model metadata contract versus clamping generated catalogs is compatibility-sensitive maintainer scope, and there are competing same-root PRs.

options.title: Fix and land this PR as canonical
options.body: Preserve audio/video in the remaining OpenAI Codex helper, keep this proof-positive smaller branch as the canonical fix, and close duplicate candidates after merge.

options.title: Port into the broader sibling
options.body: Move this PR's proof-positive loader coverage into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97858 only after that branch gets current-head real behavior proof.

options.title: Reject widening and clamp catalogs
options.body: Pause widening PRs and replace them with generated-catalog normalization that drops unsupported modalities before registry validation.

recommendation.title: Fix and land this PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Preserve audio/video in the remaining OpenAI Codex helper, keep this proof-positive smaller branch as the canonical fix, and close duplicate candidates after merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties Peter Steinberger to model catalog normalization and broader LLM/model contract surfaces involved in the compatibility choice.
